metadata.title: Parity proofs of the Kochen-Specker theorem based on the Lie algebra E8

nodes.name: Kochen-Specker theorem
nodes.statement: The Kochen-Specker theorem rules out the existence of noncontextual hidden variables theories as viable alternatives to quantum mechanics.

nodes.name: E8 root system
nodes.statement: E8 is a collection of 240 root vectors in a real 8-dimensional Euclidean space; these vectors define the vertices of the semiregular polytope $4_{21}$ discovered by Gosset.

nodes.name: 120 rays of E8
nodes.section: 2 The E8 system: rays and bases
nodes.statement: The 120 rays $|i\rangle$ ($i=1,\dots,120$) of E8 are obtained by choosing one member from each of the 120 pairs of opposite root vectors; in the Richter coordinatization with $\omega=\exp(i\pi/30)$ and $\tau=(1+\sqrt{5})/2$, each ray has eight real components.

nodes.name: Triacontagonal representation
nodes.statement: Coordinatization of E8 in which projecting the rays onto the first two coordinates places their tips at the vertices of eight regular triacontagons (30-gons) lying on concentric circles.

nodes.name: Basis (orthogonal)
nodes.statement: A basis of the E8 system is a set of eight mutually orthogonal rays of $\mathbb{R}^8$.

nodes.name: Saturated ray system
nodes.statement: A basis table is saturated if all the orthogonalities between its rays are represented in it; the saturated basis table is then equivalent to the Kochen-Specker diagram of the rays.

nodes.name: Symbol $n_{m_1}\cdots$-$B_{k}$ for ray-basis systems
nodes.statement: A system of rays and bases is denoted $n_{m_1}n'_{m_2}\cdots$-$B_{k_1}B'_{k_2}\cdots$, where the left half lists ray counts with subscripts giving multiplicities, and the right half lists basis counts with subscripts giving the number of rays per basis. E8 is denoted $120_{135}$-$2025_{8}$.

nodes.name: Letter labels A-H and basis profile
nodes.statement: The eight consecutive groups of 15 rays of E8 are labeled A,B,...,H (so A=rays 1-15, B=16-30, etc.). Each basis carries an 8-letter profile listing how its rays distribute over these triacontagons; the bases fall into 33 distinct profile families.

nodes.name: Parity proof of the KS theorem
nodes.statement: A set of projectors in a Hilbert space of even dimension is a parity proof of the KS theorem if the projectors form an odd number of bases such that each projector occurs in an even number of these bases; the impossibility of an even-odd consistent $0/1$ assignment then proves the KS theorem.

nodes.name: Critical parity proof
nodes.statement: A parity proof is critical if it ceases to be a proof of the KS theorem when even a single basis is removed from it.

nodes.name: Type 1 / Type 2 / Type 3 / Type 4 bases
nodes.statement: Type 1 bases have profile AAEEEEHH, BBFFFFGG, CCEEGGGG, or DDFFHHHH; Type 2 have AABBEEFF or CCDDGGHH; Type 3 have EEFFGGHH; Type 4 have AABBCCDD.

nodes.name: Kernaghan-Peres (KP) set
nodes.statement: A KP set is a $40_{5}$-$25_{8}$ set of 40 rays forming 25 bases with each ray occurring in five bases; constructed by Kernaghan and Peres as simultaneous eigenstates of five sets of mutually commuting three-qubit observables.

nodes.name: Pseudo KP set
nodes.statement: A pseudo KP set is a $40_{5}$-$25_{8}$ ray-basis system that resembles a KP set but is not one (some rays occur four times together with a particular companion in five bases) and admits valid noncontextual $0/1$ assignments, hence yields no proof of the KS theorem.

nodes.name: Lie algebras E7 and E6 as substructures of E8
nodes.statement: The 63 rays of E7 are those orthogonal to any chosen ray of E8 (form a saturated $63_{15}$-$135_{7}$ system); the 36 rays of E6 are those orthogonal to any two nonorthogonal rays of E8 and form no bases.

nodes.name: Basis-label generation rule
nodes.statement: $(n,m,l) = W^{n}V^{m}U^{l}(0,0,0)$ with $0\leq l\leq 14$, $0\leq m\leq 8$, $0\leq n\leq 14$, generating all 2025 bases from the seed basis.

nodes.name: Orthogonal matrix form of $U$
nodes.statement: $U = -|29\rangle\langle 1|-|115\rangle\langle 7|-|33\rangle\langle 62|+|11\rangle\langle 66|+|74\rangle\langle 70|+|61\rangle\langle 73|-|5\rangle\langle 107|-|52\rangle\langle 111|$.

nodes.name: Orthogonal matrix form of $V$
nodes.statement: $V = |5\rangle\langle 1|+|14\rangle\langle 7|-|50\rangle\langle 62|-|31\rangle\langle 66|-|22\rangle\langle 70|-|20\rangle\langle 73|-|85\rangle\langle 107|+|65\rangle\langle 111|$.

nodes.name: Orthogonal matrix form of $W$
nodes.statement: $W = |2\rangle\langle 1|+|8\rangle\langle 7|+|63\rangle\langle 62|+|67\rangle\langle 66|+|71\rangle\langle 70|+|74\rangle\langle 73|+|108\rangle\langle 107|+|112\rangle\langle 111|$.

nodes.name: General orthogonal symmetry $T$
nodes.statement: $T=(-1)^{n_{1}}|y'_{1}\rangle\langle x_{1}|+(-1)^{n_{2}}|y'_{2}\rangle\langle x_{2}|+\cdots+(-1)^{n_{8}}|y'_{8}\rangle\langle x_{8}|$, where $\{x_i\}$ and $\{y_i\}$ are bases and $n_i\in\{0,1\}$.

nodes.name: Ray-basis structure of E8
nodes.statement: Each of the 120 rays of E8 is orthogonal to 63 others and the rays form 2025 bases; each ray occurs in 135 bases, so the system is $120_{135}$-$2025_{8}$, and the basis table is saturated.
assumptions: The 120 rays of E8 in the Richter coordinatization (DP445.3)
conclusions: Each ray is orthogonal to exactly 63 others
Each ray lies in exactly 135 bases

nodes.name: Basis-table generation by $U,V,W$
nodes.statement: All 2025 bases of E8 can be generated from a single seed basis by applying products of powers of the three permutations $U,V,W$ via $(n,m,l)=W^{n}V^{m}U^{l}(0,0,0)$, with $0\leq l\leq 14$, $0\leq m\leq 8$, $0\leq n\leq 14$.
conclusions: The orbit $\{W^n V^m U^l (0,0,0)\}$ exhausts the 2025-element basis table

nodes.name: Order of the symmetry group of E8
nodes.statement: The number of orthogonal symmetries of E8 is $2025\cdot\frac{8!}{30}\cdot 2^{8}=696{,}729{,}600=192\cdot 10!$, equal to the order of the symmetry group of Gosset's polytope $4_{21}$.
assumptions: Symmetries are orthogonal transformations of the form (EP445.6) mapping bases to bases
Only $1/30$ of the $8!$ basis-label permutations extend to symmetries

nodes.name: KS theorem for E7 (proof-tree argument)
nodes.statement: The 63 rays of E7, which form a saturated $63_{15}$-$135_{7}$ system, admit no noncontextual $0/1$ assignment such that every basis has exactly one ray valued 1; hence E7 yields a proof of the KS theorem.
assumptions: Noncontextual $0/1$ value assignment with sum 1 per basis
conclusions: Therefore the KS theorem holds for E7

nodes.name: Type 1 parity proof
nodes.statement: The 15 bases with profile AAEEEEHH (and similarly for BBFFFFGG, CCEEGGGG, DDFFHHHH) form a parity proof of the KS theorem with symbol $15_{4}30_{2}$-$15_{8}$.
conclusions: Each of the four profile families yields a $15_{4}30_{2}$-$15_{8}$ parity proof

nodes.name: Additional Type 1 mixed-profile parity proofs
nodes.statement: Combining Type 1 bases of different profiles yields parity proofs with symbols $15_{4}70_{2}$-$25_{8}$ and $45_{4}50_{2}$-$35_{8}$, with 12 versions of each.

nodes.name: Type 2 parity proofs
nodes.statement: The 60 Type 2 bases (profiles AABBEEFF or CCDDGGHH) contain exactly two kinds of parity proofs: 20 versions of $36_{2}$-$9_{8}$ and 24 versions of $60_{2}$-$15_{8}$.

nodes.name: Type 3 parity proofs (60-ray $60_{6}$-$45_{8}$)
nodes.statement: The 45 Type 3 bases involve 60 rays forming a $60_{6}$-$45_{8}$ system that gives rise to 20 distinct types of parity proofs comprising 700,326 distinct versions in total.
conclusions: 20 distinct parity-proof types listed in Fig.~5

nodes.name: Type 4 parity proofs (60-ray $60_{10}$-$75_{8}$)
nodes.statement: The 75 Type 4 bases (profile AABBCCDD) involve 60 rays forming a $60_{10}$-$75_{8}$ system housing over 400 different types of parity proofs, with no critical proof exceeding 27 bases.
conclusions: More than 400 distinct parity-proof types exist
No critical parity proof has more than 27 bases

nodes.name: Most compact 8-dimensional parity proof
nodes.statement: There is a $32_{2}2_{4}$-$9_{8}$ parity proof made of 9 Type 4 bases involving only 34 rays (the proof of Fig.~9), more economical than previously known 8-dimensional KS parity proofs based on 36 rays.
conclusions: A parity proof exists with only 34 rays and 9 bases
It is more compact than the 36-ray proofs of Kernaghan-Peres (1995), Cabello (2005), and Waegell-Aravind (2012a)

nodes.name: Existence of $2^{1940}$ parity proofs in E8
nodes.statement: The E8 system contains $2^{1940}$ parity proofs of the Kochen-Specker theorem.
conclusions: $2^{1940}$ distinct parity proofs exist in E8

nodes.name: Inequality bound for basis-critical parity proofs
nodes.statement: For any basis-critical parity proof with $B$ bases, the upper bound on the corresponding inequality for any noncontextual hidden variable theory is $B-2$, while quantum mechanics predicts the value $B$, giving a universal gap of 2.

nodes.name: Pseudo KP set admits noncontextual assignment
nodes.statement: The pseudo KP set of Fig.~3b is a $40_{5}$-$25_{8}$ ray-basis system that admits valid noncontextual $0/1$ assignments, e.g. assigning 1 to rays $\{1,85,17,93,68\}$ and 0 to all others, and hence yields no proof of the KS theorem.
conclusions: The set fails to prove the KS theorem

nodes.name: Basis-table generation from a seed basis
nodes.statement: Iteratively apply powers of the three permutations $U,V,W$ to a seed basis to enumerate all 2025 bases of E8.
output: The 2025 bases $\{(n,m,l):0\leq l\leq 14,\,0\leq m\leq 8,\,0\leq n\leq 14\}$ via $(n,m,l)=W^{n}V^{m}U^{l}(0,0,0)$

nodes.name: KP set extraction from E8 basis table
nodes.statement: Construct a KP set from the bases of E8 by selecting five seed bases from one $V$-block of Fig.~2 and supplementing them with 20 bases (10 complementary pairs) chosen from the full 2025, each having four rays from one seed and four from another.
input: Five seed bases from a single $V$-block of Fig.~2 (or a $W$-translate thereof)
The full E8 basis table (2025 bases)
output: Complementary structure: 10 pairs of bases sharing no rays, each pair originating in the same pair of seed bases

nodes.name: Parity-proof extraction from a KP set
nodes.statement: Given a KP set, build parity proofs by selecting one basis from each of the 10 pairs of complementary bases and supplementing the selection with one, three, or five seed bases.
input: A KP set (DP445.12) with its 10 pairs of complementary bases and 5 seed bases
output: Up to $2^{10}=1024$ choices of complementary-pair selection, all extending to valid proofs

nodes.name: Family-restricted parity-proof search by triacontagon profile
nodes.statement: Search for parity proofs by restricting attention to bases sharing a single 8-letter triacontagon profile (one of the 33 families) instead of the full 2025-base table, dramatically reducing the search space.
input: All bases of E8 partitioned by their 8-letter A--H profile
A choice of profile family (e.g. AAEEEEHH, AABBCCDD, EEFFGGHH)
output: Critical parity proofs of the KS theorem within the chosen family
Hundreds of distinct parity-proof types of varying base counts (9 to 35) and projector ranks/multiplicities

nodes.name: Initialize seed basis
nodes.statement: Select the seed basis labeled $(0,0,0)$ corresponding to row 1 of Fig.~1.

nodes.name: Apply powers of $U$ for $l=0,\ldots,14$
nodes.statement: Generate the 15 bases $U^{l}(0,0,0)$, recovering the 15 bases of Fig.~1.

nodes.name: Apply powers of $V$ for $m=0,\ldots,8$
nodes.statement: Generate the 9 blocks $V^{m}U^{l}(0,0,0)$, producing the array of bases shown in Fig.~2.

nodes.name: Apply powers of $W$ for $n=0,\ldots,14$
nodes.statement: Generate the remaining bases $W^{n}V^{m}U^{l}(0,0,0)$, exhausting the $15\cdot 9\cdot 15=2025$ bases.

nodes.name: Pick five seed bases
nodes.statement: Select five bases from a single $V$-block of Fig.~2 (or a $W$-translate thereof).

nodes.name: Find 10 complementary pairs
nodes.statement: From the full 2025 bases, identify 20 additional bases forming 10 complementary pairs, each pair originating in the same two seed bases and sharing no rays.

nodes.name: Verify KP companion pattern
nodes.statement: Check that each ray occurs once with 17 other rays and three times with 6 other rays across the five bases it appears in; if so the construction is a genuine KP set, otherwise it is a pseudo KP set.

nodes.name: Select one basis from each complementary pair
nodes.statement: From the 10 pairs of complementary bases of the KP set, choose one member from each pair, yielding 10 bases ($2^{10}=1024$ choices).

nodes.name: Add 1, 3, or 5 seed bases
nodes.statement: Append 1, 3, or 5 of the seed bases to the 10 selected bases to obtain parity proofs with 11, 13, or 15 bases respectively.

nodes.name: Compute 8-letter profile of each basis
nodes.statement: For each basis, count the rays falling in each of the eight A--H groups and record the resulting 8-letter profile.

nodes.name: Restrict to a single profile family
nodes.statement: Select all bases sharing one chosen profile (e.g. AABBCCDD); this restricts the search space to 75 bases (Type 4) instead of 2025.

nodes.name: Search for critical parity proofs in the restricted family
nodes.statement: Within the restricted family, enumerate subsets of bases satisfying the parity condition (each ray in an even number of an odd number of bases) and discard non-critical ones.

nodes.name: Type 1 $15_{4}30_{2}$-$15_{8}$ parity proof (AAEEEEHH)
nodes.statement: Explicit list of 15 bases with profile AAEEEEHH demonstrating the $15_{4}30_{2}$-$15_{8}$ parity proof: rays 1-15 and 106-120 have multiplicity 2, rays 61-75 have multiplicity 4.

nodes.name: Two Type 2 $36_{2}$-$9_{8}$ parity proofs
nodes.statement: Two parity proofs of profile AABBEEFF or CCDDGGHH: the left can be reinterpreted as $18^{2}_{2}$-$9_{4}$ (18 rank-2 projectors), the right as $9^{2}_{2}18^{1}_{2}$-$9_{6}$ (mix of rank-1 and rank-2).

nodes.name: Type 3 $6_{6}12_{4}42_{2}$-$21_{8}$ parity proof
nodes.statement: 21 Type 3 bases (profile EEFFGGHH) with rays of multiplicity 6 (66, 81, 94, 98, 118, 119), multiplicity 4 (12 rays), and multiplicity 2 (42 rays).

nodes.name: Type 4 $36_{2}$-$9_{8}$ parity proof
nodes.statement: 9 Type 4 bases (profile AABBCCDD); 20 rays group into 10 rank-2 projectors plus 16 rank-1 projectors, giving the more descriptive symbol $10^{2}_{2}16^{1}_{2}$-$8_{6}1_{4}$.

nodes.name: Type 4 all-rank-2 $44_{2}$-$11_{8}$ parity proof
nodes.statement: 11 Type 4 bases whose 44 rays pair into 22 rank-2 projectors each occurring twice, with descriptive symbol $22^{2}_{2}$-$11_{4}$.

nodes.name: Most compact 34-ray, 9-base parity proof
nodes.statement: 9 Type 4 bases (profile AABBCCDD): rays 25 and 10 have multiplicity 4, all others multiplicity 2; the pairs (1,19),(4,55),(5,20),(16,40) define rank-2 projectors, yielding the descriptive symbol $4^{2}_{2}2^{1}_{4}24^{1}_{2}$-$8_{7}1_{8}$.

nodes.name: Kernaghan-Peres set of E8
nodes.statement: A KP $40_{5}$-$25_{8}$ set with 5 seed bases and 10 pairs of complementary bases, drawn from the top-left block of Fig.~2.

nodes.name: Pseudo KP set of E8
nodes.statement: A $40_{5}$-$25_{8}$ pseudo KP set that fails to be a KP set (rays repeat with the same companion four times) and admits a noncontextual $0/1$ assignment, hence yields no KS proof.

nodes.name: Universal hidden-variable inequality gap of 2
nodes.statement: All basis-critical parity proofs in this paper share the universal feature that quantum mechanics exceeds the noncontextual hidden-variable bound by exactly 2 (QM predicts $B$, noncontextual bound is $B-2$); the present proofs offer no advantage over earlier ones in this respect.

nodes.name: Bases not generally Pauli-eigenstates
nodes.statement: While some E8 bases (e.g. those forming KP sets) can be realized as simultaneous eigenstates of mutually commuting three-qubit Pauli observables, this is not true of E8 bases in general; an arbitrary basis is most simply generated from the computational basis by applying a product of powers of $U,V,W$.

nodes.name: Efficient quantum gates for $U,V,W$
nodes.statement: Designing efficient quantum gates that implement the unitary operators $U,V,W$ on a three-qubit system, so that arbitrary E8 bases can be experimentally generated, is an open problem.

nodes.name: Parity proofs in the remaining 29 triacontagon profiles
nodes.statement: The bases of E8 fall into 33 triacontagon profiles, of which only 4 (Types 1-4) have been explored here; the parity proofs housed by the remaining 29 profile families are unknown.

nodes.name: KS proofs from complex polytopes
nodes.statement: Whether ray systems derived from Coxeter's complex polytopes (other than Witting's polytope, the complex form of Gosset's $4_{21}$) yield new proofs of the KS theorem, and what their utility might be, remains open.
